question: What is the primary reason for keeping soiled linen away from the nurse's uniform during bed making?

options.A: To make the linen fold faster
options.B: To keep the uniform clean from starch
options.C: To comply with laundry room rules
options.D: To prevent the spread of microorganisms

explanation: Soiled linen carries microorganisms from the patient, and holding it away from the body stops cross-contamination to the nurse and the uniform. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why must bed linen be pulled tightly and kept entirely free of wrinkles?

options.A: To reduce friction and prevent pressure sores
options.B: To prevent the bed from squeaking during movement
options.C: To make the mattress look neat for visiting doctors
options.D: To help the patient stay cool in tropical climates

explanation: Wrinkles exert continuous pressure and friction on fragile skin, which significantly increases the risk of developing pressure ulcers. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h1)

question: Where should used bed linen be placed immediately after removal from a hospital bed?

options.A: Stacked neatly on the clean supply trolley
options.B: Directly onto the floor next to the bed
options.C: Over the back of a nearby wooden chair
options.D: Into a laundry hamper or moisture-proof bag

explanation: Placing used linen directly into a dedicated container prevents the environmental spread of dust and infectious organisms. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h2)

question: Which infection control practice must be observed when stripping a hospital bed?

options.A: Shaking the sheets to remove loose debris
options.B: Washing the mattress with hot oil
options.C: Using bare hands for all infectious clients
options.D: Holding soiled sheets away from the body

explanation: Keeping soiled linen away from your uniform prevents the transfer of pathogens to your clothing and subsequently to other patients. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is another common name used for an admission bed in clinical settings?
explanation: An open bed is left prepared with the top covers fan-folded down, ready to receive a newly admitted ambulatory patient. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h3)

question: How are the top covers usually arranged on an admission bed to welcome a new client?

options.A: Tucked tightly underneath the mattress at the top
options.B: Removed entirely and stored in the ward linen cupboard
options.C: Rolled tightly into a cylinder at the head of the bed
options.D: Fan-folded to the bottom or side of the bed

explanation: Fan-folding the top covers allows the incoming patient to slide easily into bed without struggling with tucked-in blankets. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which item is routinely placed near the head of an operation bed to manage post-surgical secretions?
explanation: A kidney dish is placed close by to receive emesis or oral secretions as the patient recovers from anesthesia. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h4)

question: A nurse is preparing a recovery bed for a client returning from theatre under general anesthesia. What is the main reason for fan-folding the top covers to one side?

options.A: To keep the top sheets free from surgical instrument dust
options.B: To ensure the patient can pull the blankets up independently
options.C: To allow the ward supervisor to inspect the mattress
options.D: To permit rapid and safe transfer from the stretcher

explanation: Side fan-folding leaves the bed surface clear for staff to slide the post-operative client directly from the wheeled stretcher without delay. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary clinical indication for making a cardiac bed?
explanation: Cardiac beds are tailored for clients with heart failure or breathing difficulties who require an upright position to ease breathing. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why is a foot support or rolled blanket placed at the bottom of a cardiac bed?

options.A: To prevent the client from sliding down in the upright position
options.B: To prevent the bottom sheet from bunching up near the heels
options.C: To keep the client's feet warm during cold harmattan nights
options.D: To anchor the traction weights attached to the lower limbs

explanation: Because the head of the bed is elevated significantly, gravity tends to pull the patient downward, making a foot brace necessary for stability. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h5)

question: What safety action must a nurse take immediately before starting to make a hospital bed?

options.B: Lower the bed to the floor

explanation: Locking the wheels prevents the bed from rolling away while the nurse leans against it, avoiding falls and injury. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h6)

question: Which of the following practices demonstrates proper nursing ergonomics during bed making?

options.A: Stretching across the entire mattress to pull the far sheet
options.B: Bending fully at the waist with straight knees to reach corners
options.C: Adjusting the bed to waist height before tucking in sheets
options.D: Holding heavy linen packs close to the floor while walking

explanation: Raising the bed to waist level prevents excessive spinal flexion and protects the nurse's lower back from strain. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h6)
